The card above shows the standard format of a Hong Kong Identity Card (HKID). A few key points:
ID number structure:
The number follows the pattern
X 000000 (D)
— one or two prefix letters, six digits, and a check digit in parentheses (which can be 0–9 or the letter A). For example,
A123456(3)
.
Card contents:
A real HKID includes the holder's name in both Chinese and English, sex, date of birth, date of issue, and whether the holder is a permanent resident (indicated by a star ★ symbol on the actual card).
"陳大文" (Chan Tai Man)
is a common placeholder name used in Hong Kong official examples — the equivalent of "John Doe."
The card is issued by the Hong Kong Immigration Department and is the primary identification document for residents of Hong Kong.
